source.title: Quantifying Overfitting: Evaluating Neural Network Performance through Analysis of Null Space

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is supplied
record.tranche_reason: Measures null-space angles and compares them with training–test accuracy gaps and corruption accuracy across trained image classifiers; this is a different measure aimed at generalization and overfitting.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on overfitting measures and generalization under data corruptions. Its claims about random-label fitting and generalization mechanisms, optimizer, batch size, and dropout effects are not tested here. Corruption accuracy concerns distribution shifts and does not directly test same-distribution generalization versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates null-space angle scores as proxies for overfitting and corruption robustness. It does not measure magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness or test any other listed version. Dropout and augmentation vary across training runs, but the paper does not identify controlled comparisons or attribute held-out accuracy differences to dropout.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as an account of the authors' conclusion: they claim that last-layer null-space and target-class angles, computed using a small test subset without training-data access, quantify overfitting and indicate corruption generalization across evaluated classifiers. The reported associations do not establish guaranteed detection of overfitting or protection against privacy leakage.
record.recipe_differences: Uses last-layer null-space and class-weight angle measures, and evaluates accuracy on corruption-shifted test data; does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported patterns vary across models, datasets, and architectures; CIFAR100 results use only incorrectly predicted samples for the stated ablation analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors propose O = α + β as an overfitting score. Table 1 reports CIFAR10 ResNet18 training–test accuracy gaps of 0.25–15.96 percentage points, but the score does not consistently rank those gaps: model 8 has O = 51.54 and gap 2.07, whereas model 1 has O = 32.32 and gap 5.21.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-layer representation angles provide a proposed proxy for overfitting; their correspondence with training–test accuracy gaps is imperfect.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report alignment between normalized angle score G and corruption accuracy on CIFAR10 and SVHN. Table 2 gives CIFAR10 model 1 G = 1.7563 and corruption accuracy 55.128%, versus model 2 G = 1.4234 and 35.666%. These are distribution-shift evaluations rather than tests of the listed interventions or sharpness measure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A normalized null-space angle score can track corruption robustness among the evaluated classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 reports that average target-label softmax and logit outputs can fail to distinguish overfitting. In Table 1, model 1 has higher softmax confidence than model 2 despite a smaller training–test accuracy gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average prediction confidence need not rank classifiers by their training–test accuracy gaps.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says source code will be available after review
record.problems: The paper does not report uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Its main-text evidence is limited to 11 ResNet18 models on CIFAR10, with additional tables for other datasets and architectures. The generalization comparison uses data corruptions, which are distribution shifts rather than same-distribution held-out examples. Training recipes vary, and the paper gives limited detail about their settings.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly test any of the eight claim versions, so no rows qualify. Corruption accuracy and the proposed angle metrics are reported, but those outcomes concern distribution-shift performance or measurement of a proxy rather than the versions' named behaviors.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level random-label test accuracy alongside natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Held-out error changes attributable to dropout, including training-set size, dropout strength, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Null-space angles are a different construct from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Keeping the result rows and version verdicts empty is appropriate; the omitted proxy and corruption results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
